title: The New Scientific Method  -  Housed in the 7Q Framework

canonical_node.axiom: Truth emerges from destruction, not confirmation; inquiry must include the why layer and epistemic humility.
definitions: Destruction-first: starting inquiry by attempting to falsify all plausible models.
Why layer: formal inquiry into mechanistic, statistical, teleological, constraint, and ontological causes.
Q0: the precondition that the inquirer cannot be the ground of inquiry; arrive with humility.
Model death: a model is provisionally accepted only if it survives all attempts to kill it.
Cross-domain coherence: a model must hold across physics, mathematics, logic, information theory, and metaphysics.
derivation: The traditional method asks WHAT and HOW but never formally asks WHY, creating a structural gap.
Historical evidence shows breakthroughs came from asking why; dead frameworks refused to ask why.
The 7Q framework provides forward (investigate) and reverse (prove) directions that incorporate destruction-first and why.
The anchoring principle: the model that survives the most attempts to kill it is provisionally accepted, not proven.
The method adds Q0, five death conditions, multi-dimensional evaluation, and a meta-layer for auditing.
canonical_node.action: When conducting scientific inquiry, generate competing models, attempt to falsify them, ask why at multiple levels, check cross-domain coherence, and maintain epistemic humility.
boundary: Does not claim to replace all scientific practice; it is a framework for inquiry.
Does not guarantee that asking why will produce breakthroughs.
Does not provide a formal algorithm for generating models or testing them.
Does not claim that teleological or ontological why answers are always testable.
test: Check that inquiry starts with destruction, not confirmation.
Check that multiple competing models are generated and tested.
Check that the why layer is explicitly addressed (mechanistic, statistical, teleological, constraint, ontological).
Check that cross-domain coherence is evaluated.
Check that Q0 humility is acknowledged.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a destruction-first, why-inclusive scientific method framework that formalizes model competition and epistemic humility.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the core of empirical testing and falsification, but expands it to include multiple death conditions and cross-domain coherence.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the framework loses its distinctive destruction-first and why-inclusive approach, reverting to a more traditional hypothesis-confirmation method.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as a methodological proposal; do not treat as empirically verified

overstatement_risks: Claims historical evidence demonstrates that asking why is the engine of discovery, but this is an interpretation, not a controlled study.
Claims the traditional method has no why layer, but some fields do address why informally.
Claims the new method closes the gap, but it does not provide a formal proof of efficacy.
kill_conditions: If the why layer admits untestable speculative answers without constraint.
If the method fails to produce better scientific outcomes in practice.
If the historical evidence is shown to be cherry-picked or misrepresented.
risk.lean_target: A methodological proposal for destruction-first, why-inclusive inquiry; not a proven replacement for the scientific method.

plain_summary: This document proposes a new scientific method based on the 7Q framework, emphasizing destruction-first inquiry, mandatory model competition, and a formal why layer. It argues that the traditional method's avoidance of why is a structural gap and that asking why drives breakthroughs. The method includes Q0 humility, five death conditions, multi-dimensional evaluation, and cross-domain coherence. However, it is a proposal, not an empirically validated method, and its historical claims are interpretive.
